# Template: galton_board
A Galton board (bean machine): rows of pegs in a triangle, bins below filled to exact binomial heights — randomness in each bounce, yet the bell shape every time — with an optional single highlighted ball path and an optional normal curve drawn over the bins. Choose this scene for ANY request about the Galton board or bean machine, why random events make a bell curve, the binomial distribution becoming normal, or "order out of randomness".
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "rows": {
   "type": "integer",
   "minimum": 4,
   "maximum": 12,
   "description": "Peg rows, 4-12 (default 8)."
  },
  "show_path": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "One highlighted ball's bouncing path from the top into a bin (default true)."
  },
  "show_curve": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Normal curve drawn over the bin tops — the reveal (default false)."
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string"
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- pegs: the peg triangle (a group)
- bin_<k>: bin k's outline and fill (a group), left to right
- path: the highlighted ball path (when show_path)
- curve: the normal curve over the bins (when show_curve)
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Draw a Galton board and show how the bins fill into a bell shape." → params: {"show_curve":true,"title":"Order out of randomness"}
Request: "Show one ball bouncing down a Galton board." → params: {"rows":6,"title":"One ball, many choices"}

In YAML: `template: galton_board` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
